thread:
incident-bot: HIGH - possible cross-tenant artifact observed on dedicated pool kestrel-dedicated-3. Alert rule: `kestrel::cache-prefix-collision > 0.9`. Sample evidence attached (log excerpts). Paging oncall.
oncall-jess: Acked. I’m on pager. Jumping in now — tagging eng and infra. @eng-aaron @infra-maria can you pull the live audit and surface any overlapping cache keys or ip mappings? :rotating_light:
eng-aaron: pulling logs now. running query against cache audit index. snippet: ```
# found entries where tenant_id != owner_tenant and kv_prefix == /cust-KestrelCorp/session/
select ts, node, tenant_id, owner_tenant, key from cache_audit where key like '%/cust-KestrelCorp/session/%' limit 50;
``` results look odd — 3 hits on node gpu-42 showing owner_tenant = cust-kestrelcorp but tenant_id = cust-lyra. Investigating if it's read-only echo or full exposure.
infra-maria: checking routing and pool assignment. kube: `kubectl get pods -n dedicated-kestrel -o wide` shows pod eviction events in the last 10m on gpu-42. Also seeing a stray iptable rule reapply job executed ~2165431980 by autoscaler. Could be transient namespace cleanup race.
oncall-jess: If there's cross-tenant reads, we need quick isolation. Do we have a safe mitigation that preserves customer throughput? Options: 1) soft-evict node gpu-42 from pool, drain connections; 2) flip pool to read-only for a minute; 3) apply ACLs on the KV cache layer. What’s fastest?
eng-aaron: fastest is to cordon+drain gpu-42 and force point-eviction of cache shards on that node. Command: ```
kubectl cordon gpu-42 && kubectl drain gpu-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
# then
rdctl cache scrub --node gpu-42 --prefix '/cust-KestrelCorp/session/' --dry-run
``` Doing cordon now.
infra-maria: I can flip pool routing to fallback pool kestrel-dedicated-1 for new requests: ```
api: POST /v1/routing/pools/kestrel-dedicated-3/override
body: { "route_to": "kestrel-dedicated-1", "reason": "isolation - possible cache collision" }
``` That reroutes traffic instantly. Prepare rollback. 
sre-olivia: Oncall handoff scheduled? I can take post-mitigation verification once node is drained. Also run data-integrity checks across tenants for the last 24h. Assigning tasks: eng-aaron -> live audit + scrub, infra-maria -> node drain & routing override, security-nina -> quick forensics on replicas and ACL logs, cs-luis -> customer comms.
customer-success-luis: Notifying KestrelCorp primary contact (kestrel-ops@cust.com) with a short heads-up: "We are investigating an internal cache routing anomaly affecting your dedicated pool. We may route traffic to another pool temporarily. Will update within 30 minutes." Sending now. :email:
oncall-jess: Update: cordon succeeded, drain in progress (evicting 12 connections). ETA ~90s.
eng-aaron: scrub dry-run shows 3 keys that would be removed on gpu-42 belonging to cust-KestrelCorp but present under cust-lyra tenant reads. This looks like stale shard reattachment, not remote write. Starting actual scrub now. ```
rdctl cache scrub --node gpu-42 --prefix '/cust-KestrelCorp/session/' --confirm
``` results: 3 keys removed. Logging to evidence bucket s3://redwood-incidents/2165432100/scrub.log
security-nina: Pulling ACL and replication logs. No external exfil events detected (no outbound egress to unknown hosts). Replication shows one accelerated shard reassign at 2165431968 that coincides with autoscaler job. Capturing snapshot for deeper forensics.
infra-maria: Routing override applied at 2165432050. New requests now routed to kestrel-dedicated-1. Rolling back autoscaler job that re-applied iptables at 2165431980 — disabling that particular hook until we patch.
oncall-jess: Customer updated: "We've temporarily routed traffic to another pool while we verify isolation. No confirmed data leakage to third parties. We will update within 60 minutes after audit." Got ack from cust. KestrelCorp asked for timeline; told them ~2h preliminary and full report next business day.
eng-aaron: Post-scrub verification: re-run audit query across last 2h, no remaining cross-tenant hits. ```
select count(*) from cache_audit where key like '%/cust-KestrelCorp/%' and tenant_id != owner_tenant and ts > 2165430000;
# result: 0
```
sre-olivia: Taking over from oncall-jess for follow-up. I'll keep a watch for 2h and coordinate with infra to reintroduce gpu-42 after patch. Creating incident runbook ticket: INC-2165432100. Assigning postmortem: eng-aaron (owner), infra-maria (patch), security-nina (forensics), cs-luis (customer comms).
security-nina: Initial severity assessment: P1 -> downgraded to P2 because no evidence of exfil beyond intra-cluster artifact; impact limited to internal stale cache exposure. Recommend notification to compliance and to run full kv-check against last 7 days.
customer-success-luis: Sent customer follow-up: "Preliminary investigation indicates stale cache entries were served across tenant namespaces on a single drained node; we removed the entries and routed traffic away. No evidence of data export. We will share a full timeline and mitigations ASAP." Customer replied with :thumbsup: and asked to be looped in on the postmortem.
oncall-jess: Marking this thread solved for immediate mitigation. Leaving handoff notes: gpu-42 quarantined, routing override active, scrubbed 3 keys, autoscaler iptables hook disabled. Follow-up tasks created in INC-2165432100.
sre-olivia: Will run deeper consistency and KV reconciliation. Expecting to reintroduce node after kernel-level iptables patch + additional guardrail. ETA reintroduce 4-6 hours contingent on tests.
eng-aaron: Adding a short-term guard: on new pool creations, enforce stricter shard attach verification and add a 30s cooling window before iptables/iptables-reapply hooks run. Pushing PR for autoscaler hook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/987
security-nina: For record: collecting evidence bundle and preserving chain-of-custody in case of compliance request. Upload path: s3://redwood-incidents/2165432100/evidence.tar.gz
customer-success-luis: Customer asked for the scrub log and we shared scrub.log (redacted). They confirmed they will review and asked to be informed when postmortem published.
sre-olivia: Closing notes: owner eng-aaron to draft postmortem with timeline, root-cause hypothesis is shard reattachment race during autoscaler iptables reapply. Mitigations: immediate node quarantine, scrub, routing override, disable hook; medium-term: autoscaler patch + shard attach verification; long-term: enhance pool-level guardrails and add automated anomaly detection to catch prefix collisions earlier.
oncall-jess: Thanks team. Leaving the channel. :eyes:
incident-bot: Incident status updated to MONITORED at 2165432389. Incident INC-2165432100 created and assigned.
